diagram_classification: cosmological (probable); a schematic of interlaced concentric circles, possibly planetary or celestial spheres
interpretation: The diagram shows an empty central circle surrounded by several concentric rings. Bands that look woven over and under each other cross these rings, and an outer circle encloses the whole figure. The most plausible reading is a schematic of a cosmos of nested, interacting orbits or spheres. The empty centre would stand for the Earth or the fixed point of the system, and the interlaced bands for the crossing paths of planets or celestial circles, or for the mutual bonds that hold the elements and spheres together. A less likely alternative is a purely ornamental or symbolic interlace, such as a figure of unity or cosmic harmony, in the manner of early medieval knotwork. No labels, names or numbers can be read in the figure, so no specific cosmological model can be identified.
evidence: Visible: a plain central circle, concentric rings, bands drawn as alternately passing over and under each other, a double outer boundary, red-brown ink on parchment, and no legible inscriptions inside the figure. The text visible on the page is only show-through or surrounding text and is not part of the diagram. External: medieval cosmological and computistical manuscripts often use concentric circles for planetary spheres or the elements, and interlace patterns appear in early medieval art. Because there are no labels and no named source can be tied to the figure, the cosmological classification is tentative and the specific meaning of the interlacing is uninterpreted.
